name: Muse Wonder
archDisplay: Proprietary multimodal reasoning model (architecture undisclosed); 1M-token context, trained for long-running personal and professional agent work
note: Meta's first frontier-tier model, released October 12, 2026 in the Meta Model API (muse-wonder-1.0) and Muse Code at $4/$20 per Mtok ($0.20 cached input), four times Muse Spark 1.3's price. Meta's own scorecard puts it level with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra rather than ahead: it leads DeepSWE 1.1 (78.8) and Meta's internal MemoryBench, trails Opus 5.5 on HealthBench Pro, OSWorld and Terminal-Bench 4.0. Independent rows here come from Vals AI's launch-day run (Vals Index 61.06%, #10 of 47; #1 on CyberBench v1.1). NOT FILED: Meta's Personal Superintelligence Index (54.3) and MemoryBench (85.6) are internal composites; Harvey LAB-AA (10.0) is Artificial Analysis's v1.1 re-grading with hallucination checks, not the Vals-run harvey-legal-agent column; AutomationBench-AA (39.1) is AA's variant, not Zapier's private-set AutomationBench column; ProgramBench (50.0) uses a >=95%-tests-passing metric that disagrees with Vals' ProgramBench scale; Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3 is 52 (no corpus column).

results.notes: Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, Vals AI launch-day evaluation (±3.10, #8 of 79). Meta's scorecard reports the different Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 (10.0), not filed.
Vals Finance Agent v2, Vals AI evaluation (±0.38, #16 of 78); matches the 56.6 on Meta's scorecard.
Terminal-Bench 4.0, Vals AI evaluation (±2.20, #9 of 47). Meta's scorecard cites Artificial Analysis's run at 52.0.

DeepSWE v1.1, Meta's launch scorecard on dev.meta.ai (max reasoning effort; peers GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 also at max); Meta cites Datacurve's third-party run. Ahead of Opus 5.5 (74.2) and GPT-6 Astra (74.1).

JobBench, Meta's launch scorecard on dev.meta.ai (max reasoning effort; peers GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 also at max); behind Opus 5.5 (75.4) and Fable 5.1 (73.1).
